description.la: Constitutiones quarti concilii Lateranensis (1215) sub Innocentio III, a Firmiter credimus (de fide catholica) ad constitutionem de Terra Sancta.
description.en-US: The seventy-one constitutions of the twelfth ecumenical council, held at the Lateran in 1215 under Innocent III: the profession of faith Firmiter credimus (with the definition of transubstantiation), the condemnation of Joachim of Fiore and the Albigensians, annual confession and Easter communion, the reform of the clergy and the preparation of the Fifth Crusade. Latin text with Schroeder's English (1937).
description.pt-BR: As setenta e uma constituições do décimo segundo concílio ecumênico, reunido no Latrão em 1215 sob Inocêncio III: a profissão de fé Firmiter credimus, com a definição da transubstanciação, a confissão anual e a comunhão pascal, a reforma do clero e a cruzada.

la.editor: Conciliorum Oecumenicorum Decreta (Bologna 1962), via Latin Wikisource / Documenta Catholica Omnia

sources.edition: Latin Wikisource, Concilium Lateranum IV, the text of Conciliorum Oecumenicorum Decreta (Bologna 1962) as circulated by Documenta Catholica Omnia. Wikitext fetched through action=raw.
sources.description: Complete as transcribed. The digitisation has its punctuation largely stripped, no capitals at the start of sentences, lowercase deus/dominus, and no canon numbers; the text is left as transcribed, with line breaks kept as paragraph breaks, the digitisation's split enclitics rejoined ("ideo que" → "ideoque") and bracketed headings turned into markdown headings. The English of Schroeder (1937) numbers the canons.
sources.tierEvidence: Medieval documents; the digitisation derives from the Library of Latin Texts / COD text (a critical edition of 1962/1973), which carries at most a neighbouring right that has run out and is freely redistributed by Wikisource and Documenta Catholica Omnia.

sources.edition: H. J. Schroeder, O.P., Disciplinary Decrees of the General Councils: Text, Translation and Commentary, St. Louis and London: B. Herder, 1937. archive.org OCR (schroeder-disciplinary-councils_djvu.txt).
sources.description: For each canon Schroeder's one-sentence summary (in italics) and the translated text. Schroeder's historical introduction, his comments and his footnotes are not included, and the OCR's running heads and page-end footnotes were stripped by script (research/sourcing/_scripts/councils_schroeder.py); a few inline footnote marks and OCR slips remain. Schroeder translates the disciplinary decrees only.
sources.tierEvidence: Published 1937; US copyright not renewed (confirmed by TAN Books, which holds the Herder list); Schroeder died in 1942.
